'''Stanley George Wojcicki'''<ref name=bookref1>{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZZxmAAAAMAAJ&q=%22WOJCICKI%2C+STANLEY+GEORGE+physicist%2C+educator%22| title=Who's who in the West| volume=31| year=2004| publisher=[[Marquis Who's Who, Incorporated]]| isbn=9780837909356}}</ref> ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|v|uː|ɪ|ˈ|tʃ|ɪ|t|s|k|i}} {{respell|VOO|ih|CHITS|kee}};<ref>{{YouTube|wC0ezsf_zLM|"2016 Breakthrough Prize Symposium: Introducing the 2016 Laureates in Fundamental Physics"}}</ref> born '''Stanisław Jerzy Wójcicki''', {{IPA|pl|vujˈt͡ɕit͡skʲi|lang}}; March 30, 1937 – May 31, 2023)<ref>[https://paloaltoonline.com/news/2023/06/07/world-renowned-physicist-stanley-wojcicki-dies-at-86 World-renowned physicist Stanley Wojcicki dies at 86]</ref> was an American physicist and former chair of the [[physics]] department at [[Stanford University]] in California.<ref>{{cite web
| title = Stanley Wojcicki - Stanford University Physics Faculty page
| url = http://www.stanford.edu/dept/physics/people/faculty/wojcicki_stanley.html
| date = 
| accessdate = July 8, 2012}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Wojcicki was born in [[Warsaw]], Poland, the son of [[Janina Wójcicka Hoskins|Janina Wanda Wójcicka]] (née Kozłowska), a bibliographer, and [[Franciszek Wójcicki]], a lawyer.<ref name=bookref1/><ref>{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TG9pAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Bom+Janina+Wanda+Ewa+Kozlow%22| title=The Polish Review| publisher=Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences in America| year=1997| volume=42| page=123}}</ref> He and his brother fled from Poland to Sweden with his mother at the age of 12, when [[People's Republic of Poland|communists]] came to power.<ref name="sfgate2013">{{cite news|url=http://www.sfgate.com/bayarea/article/Bay-Area-s-Wojcicki-family-honored-4415518.php |title=Bay Area's Wojcicki family honored |newspaper=San Francisco Chronicle |date=April 6, 2013 |first=Julian |last=Guthrie |accessdate=October 4, 2014 }}</ref> They eventually arrived in the United States. His father remained in Poland, and was soon imprisoned for five years for being a member of the government's main opposition party. He was never able to gain a visa to come to the United States.<ref name="sfgate2013"/>

Wojcicki and his brother were sent to a boarding school run by the [[Order of Friars Minor|Franciscan Order]] near [[Buffalo, New York]].<ref name="sfgate2013"/> He excelled in mathematics and had thought of pursuing either engineering or medicine, but decided to study physics. He attended [[Harvard University]] on a scholarship and graduated with a BA. He later attended the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he earned a PhD.<ref name=endowed>[http://www.stanford.edu/dept/physics/people/endow.html#wojcicki Stanford Department of Physics: "Endowed Chairs and Professorships: Stanley G. Wojcicki Chair in Physics: First Endowed Chair in Experimental Physics Honors Beloved Professor"] retrieved September 22, 2012</ref>

==Career==
Wojcicki worked at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] and was a [[National Science Foundation]] fellow at [[CERN]] and the [[Collège de France]]. In 1966, he joined the [[Stanford University]] physics faculty where he headed the Department of Physics from 1982–1985 and 2004–2007.<ref name=endowed />

Wojcicki served as an advisor to government funding agencies (US and foreign) as well as to several high energy physics laboratories. He also headed the [[High Energy Physics Advisory Panel]], which advises the [[United States Department of Energy]] and the National Science Foundation on particle physics matters.<ref name=endowed />

Wojcicki led the HEPAP subpanel New Facilities for the US High-Energy Physics Program which recommended building the [[Superconducting Super Collider|Super Conducting Super Collilder]] in 1983.<ref>{{Cite book|author1-link=Michael Riordan (physicist) |last=Riordan |first=Michael |title=Tunnel visions : the rise and fall of the superconducting super collider |date=2015 |author2=Lillian Hoddeson|author2-link=Lillian Hoddeson |author3-link=Adrienne Kolb|author3=Adrienne W. Kolb |isbn=978-0-226-29479-7 |location=Chicago |pages=22 |oclc=907132862}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wojcicki |first=Stanley |date=January 2008 |title=The Supercollider: The Pre-Texas Days — A Personal Recollection of Its Birth and Berkeley Years |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S1793626808000113 |journal=Reviews of Accelerator Science and Technology |language=en |volume=01 |issue=1 |pages=259–302 |doi=10.1142/S1793626808000113 |issn=1793-6268|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Stanley Wojcicki was the husband of fellow educator [[Esther Wojcicki]], whom he met at UC Berkeley, and married in 1962.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 4, 1962 |title=Miss Hochman Becomes Mrs. Stanley Wojcicki |work=Valley Times |page=8 |volume=25 |issue=4}}</ref> They had three children and ten grandchildren.<ref name=huffington>[http://www.huffingtonpost.com/esther-wojcicki# Esther Wojcicki] retrieved September 21, 2012</ref>
*[[Susan Wojcicki]], former CEO of YouTube.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://variety.com/2014/digital/news/google-to-name-susan-wojcicki-head-of-youtube-reports-1201087575/|title = Google Names Susan Wojcicki CEO of YouTube|accessdate = February 5, 2014|website = Variety| date=February 5, 2014 }}</ref> [[History of Google|Google's first office]] was started in her home.<ref name=endowed /><ref name=huffington /><ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/tech/techinvestor/corporatenews/2007-07-04-google-wojcicki_N.htm USA Today: "The house that helped build Google" By Jefferson Graham] July 5, 2007</ref>
*Janet Wojcicki, assistant professor of pediatrics at UCSF.<ref name=huffington />
*[[Anne Wojcicki]], founder and CEO of the [[genetic testing]] company [[23andMe]]<ref name=huffington />

In 2010, his daughter Anne and her then-husband, Google co-founder [[Sergey Brin]], endowed a $2.5 million chair in experimental physics at Stanford in her father's name.<ref name=endowed />

Wojcicki was a [[Catholic Church|Catholic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 1, 2019 |title=Q&A: Esther Wojcicki raised the CEO of YouTube, the CEO of 23andMe and a doctor. Here are her 5 rules for successful parenting |url=https://www.deseret.com/2019/6/1/20674637/q-a-esther-wojcicki-raised-the-ceo-of-youtube-the-ceo-of-23andme-and-a-doctor-here-are-her-5-rules-f |access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=Deseret News |language=en}}</ref>

Wojcicki died at his residence in [[Los Altos, California]], on May 31, 2023, at the age of 86.<ref>{{cite news|url = https://physics.stanford.edu/news/professor-stanley-wojcicki-has-died-age-86|title = Professor Stanley Wojcicki has died at age 86|website = [[Stanford University]]|date = June 5, 2023|accessdate = August 10, 2024}}</ref>
